name: Choosing Symbol Pairs
description: There is a given string S consisting of N symbols. Your task is to find the number of ordered pairs of integers i and j such that 1. 1 ≤ i , j ≤ N 2. S [ i ] = S [ j ] , that is the i -th symbol of string S is equal to the j -th.
input_specification: The single input line contains S , consisting of lowercase Latin letters and digits. It is guaranteed that string S in not empty and its length does not exceed 10 5 .
output_specification: Print a single number which represents the number of pairs i and j with the needed property. Pairs ( x , y ) and ( y , x ) should be considered different, i.e. the ordered pairs count.
subsubtopic: 406. Knuth Morris Pratt (KMP) and Prefix Automaton
approach_summary: Precompute the prefix function π[i] matching longest proper prefix-suffix in O(M). Traverse text string with π transitions to locate all occurrences in O(N) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 50B — Choosing Symbol Pairs [406. Knuth Morris Pratt (KMP) and Prefix Automaton]
topic_editorial.summary: String matching with prefix automaton / KMP.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The prefix function $\pi[i]$ defines the length of the longest proper prefix of $S[0..i]$ that is also a suffix of $S[0..i]$. When a mismatch occurs at index $j$, we do not backtrack in text; we jump to $\pi[j-1]$, preserving previously matched characters.
